passage: I'm Sarika. When Irawati became our team lead in March, I was the first to hug her. By June something had shifted. She interrupted me twice in one stand-up, finished my sentences wrong, and began expecting the corner parking spot and first pick of leave dates. The others muttered about it in the pantry. I didn't join in, though I was tempted. I also knew her targets had doubled and her own boss called her at night. So one evening, walking to the bus stop, I said, "Ira, you've been cutting people off lately. I think the pressure's getting to you, but it's landing on us." She was quiet for a long stretch. Then: "I didn't realise. Will you tell me when I do it?" Looking back, I'm glad I said it to her and not about her.

qa.q: When did Irawati become the team lead?
qa.a: Irawati became our team lead in March.

qa.q: Why didn't Sarika join the muttering in the pantry?
qa.a: Sarika was tempted but felt sympathy for Irawati, knowing her targets had doubled and her boss called her at night.

qa.q: What choice did Sarika make on the walk to the bus stop, and why did it work?
qa.a: Sarika named the interrupting directly and kindly to Irawati while mentioning the pressure, so Irawati could hear it and asked to be told next time.

qa.q: How might Irawati have felt hearing about the change?
qa.a: Irawati was probably surprised and a little stung, going quiet, but also open enough to ask Sarika to tell her when it happens 🙂

grounding: Shows a colleague noticing a friend-turned-manager interrupting and taking perks, and naming it gently while crediting the pressure.

passage:
Note, 14 Aug. Devika, Class 3 teacher.
Manjula took over as primary coordinator in June. Things I've noticed since, written down so I don't turn them into staffroom gossip: she cut Rekha off mid-sentence twice at Monday's meeting; she no longer asks us before changing the exam timetable; yesterday she sent the peon to fetch her lunch first, ahead of everyone. The Manjula who shared my tiffin last year would have hated that. I also know the principal emails her at midnight and parents call her personal number.
What I did next: I asked her for tea after school, just the two of us. I said, "You've been interrupting people lately, and it's being noticed. I know you're being squeezed from above." She teared up a little, then laughed. She's asked me to nudge her ankle under the table at the next meeting.

qa.q: When did Manjula take over as primary coordinator?
qa.a: Manjula took over as primary coordinator in June.

qa.q: Why did Devika write the changes down?
qa.a: Devika wanted to keep track of what had changed without turning it into staffroom gossip, which shows a wish to be fair to Manjula.

qa.q: Which choice did Devika make instead of complaining, and how did it land?
qa.a: Devika asked Manjula for tea alone and named the interrupting while acknowledging the pressure; Manjula teared up, laughed, and asked for a nudge under the table.

qa.q: What is it like for Rekha when Manjula cuts in mid-sentence?
qa.a: Rekha is likely to feel brushed aside and less willing to speak at meetings, which is part of why Devika's note matters.

grounding: A teacher's note records a friend-turned-coordinator starting to interrupt and expect special treatment, and a gentle private conversation.

passage:
12 Nov. Long day. Rajni's been floor manager for two months and today it really showed. In the huddle she talked over Gurpreet three times and then said, "Let's not waste time on feelings." She also took the window seat by the heater again, the one we used to take turns on. Old Rajni would have rolled her eyes at a manager like this. Ankit tried to get me to moan about her at the chai stall. I didn't. It's not fair either; she has the quality team breathing down her neck and a target that keeps going up. So at clock-out I waited and said, "Raj, you've stopped listening a bit. I get the pressure. I just miss you asking." She went quiet, then said, "Okay. Ouch. Fair." We shared an auto home. I think it landed.
— Jasleen

qa.q: What did Rajni say in the huddle?
qa.a: Rajni said, "Let's not waste time on feelings."

qa.q: How does Jasleen feel about the change in Rajni, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Jasleen misses the old Rajni, saying "I just miss you asking", but also feels for Rajni under pressure from the quality team.

qa.q: What did Jasleen choose at clock-out, and why was the timing wise?
qa.a: Jasleen waited and spoke to Rajni alone, naming the change and the pressure, so it felt private and caring rather than public.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet see that huddle?
qa.a: Gurpreet might feel talked over and dismissed, especially after being told not to waste time on feelings 😔

grounding: Shows a peer noticing a friend-turned-floor-manager stop listening and claim perks, and raising it gently instead of gossiping.

passage:
Kunal: Samir, got 5 min?
Samir: busy but go
Kunal: as a friend, not your team member. can I say something?
Samir: ok now I'm nervous
Kunal: since you became manager, you've changed a bit. you cut Priya off twice in today's meeting
Kunal: and you asked me to get your coffee in front of the new guys
Samir: I was joking about the coffee
Kunal: I know. didn't land like a joke though
Samir: wow ok
Kunal: I'm not saying this to the others. I'd rather say it to you
Kunal: and I know the targets are crazy and your boss calls you at 10pm. I see that too
Samir: they really are
Samir: I didn't notice the Priya thing
Kunal: I think the pressure's making you rush people
Samir: ...fair. I'll say sorry to her tomorrow
Samir: and tell me if I do it again? 🙏
Kunal: deal. and I'll get my own coffee 🙂

qa.q: Who did Samir cut off twice in the meeting?
qa.a: Samir cut Priya off twice in today's meeting.

qa.q: What does Samir's 'ok now I'm nervous' suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Samir senses something uncomfortable is coming and is a bit anxious about what Kunal will say.

qa.q: Which choice by Kunal helped the message land?
qa.a: Speaking to Samir directly instead of the others, and admitting the pressure Samir is under, let Samir hear it without feeling attacked.

qa.q: How might Priya feel if Samir apologises tomorrow?
qa.a: Priya might feel relieved and respected, and more willing to speak up in meetings again.

grounding: A colleague notices a friend who became manager interrupting and expecting favours, and names it gently while acknowledging the pressure.

passage: At the milk cooperative in Wadgaon, Yusuf had always been the joker who helped everyone carry the cans. Then, at twenty-five, he was made collection-centre supervisor. Reena, who tested fat content at the next table, watched him change over two months. He began cutting farmers off mid-sentence when they queried a reading. He expected the first glass of tea from the stall boy, before the women who had been standing since five. In the meeting he talked over her twice. The other staff whispered about it by the chilling tank. Reena didn't join them. She also knew the dairy board now phoned him every evening about falling numbers. One afternoon, walking to the bus stand, she said, "Yusuf, you've stopped letting people finish. I think the board's pressure is getting to you, but the farmers feel it." He was quiet for a long time. Then he said, "Stop me when I do it."

qa.q: What was Reena's job at the cooperative?
qa.a: She tested fat content at the next table.

qa.q: What was Reena thinking when she chose not to join the whispers?
qa.a: She saw Yusuf's rudeness but also knew the dairy board's pressure on him, so she wanted to help him change rather than gossip.

qa.q: What did Reena do well when she spoke to Yusuf?
qa.a: She named one clear behaviour, linked it to the pressure he was under, and said it privately on the walk, so he could listen without losing face.

qa.q: How do the farmers experience Yusuf's change?
qa.a: They are cut off when they question a reading and see the women who waited since five served tea last, which likely feels unfair and disrespectful.

grounding: A colleague notices a friend-turned-supervisor interrupting and expecting special treatment, and gently names it while recognising the pressure on him.
